threshold_rationale: Recall-oriented; prioritizes catching defaulters over false-positive rate, given asymmetric cost of missed defaults vs. declined good applicants

calibration.uncalibrated_finding: Raw XGBoost probabilities were severely overconfident due to scale_pos_weight (e.g. predicted 0.86 vs actual 0.37 in top decile)
calibration.recommendation: Use xgb_final_model.pkl (raw) for ranking/classification; use xgb_calibrated_model.pkl for any use case requiring trustworthy probability values (e.g. expected loss calculations)
calibration.threshold_rationale: Recall-oriented threshold on calibrated probabilities, chosen to match the same ~80-88% defaulter-recall philosophy as the uncalibrated 0.30 threshold, now expressed in honest probability terms (0.05 predicted probability here corresponds to real ~5-18% risk, not the inflated values the raw model would have shown)

cost_based_threshold_analysis.method: Minimized total cost = (false_negatives * cost_ratio) + false_positives, cost_ratio = FN_cost / FP_cost

primary_recommendation.rationale: Cost ratio of 5:1 (missed default costs 5x a wrongly-declined applicant) is a commonly cited reference point in credit risk literature; actual ratio should be tuned to real loan amounts, interest margins, and recovery rates once available.

cost_based_threshold_analysis.note: This cost-based threshold (0.71) is notably more conservative than the earlier recall-oriented threshold (0.30) chosen without formal cost modeling — illustrating why formal cost analysis matters over intuition alone.

cross_validation.finding: XGBoost and Random Forest performance is statistically indistinguishable under 5-fold CV. Single-split advantage for XGBoost did not replicate.
